title: Field-craft runbook for cost ops: operationalizing batching, caching and safe quantization
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Objective: produce a pragmatic, field-tested runbook that enables platform and SRE teams to deploy cost-saving inference controls (dynamic batching, prefix/KV caching, and conservative quantization profiles) with measurable guardrails for latency and quality. Hypothesis: by surfacing a prescriptive set of configuration patterns, rollout steps, and automated checks, we can capture >=15% token-cost reduction on target chat workloads without exceeding 10% latency tail regression or 1.5% quality drift on tracked prompts. Scope: playbook content, experiment recipes, rollout checklist, alerting rules, dashboards, and two pilot rollouts (one hosted API product path and one Dedicated customer path). Out-of-scope: model architecture changes, custom compiler kernels, and billing model changes.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook doc published in Confluence with step-by-step rollout and rollback guidance
Two pilot rollouts completed and post-mortem documented (hosted + dedicated)
Automated gating rules implemented in Console for latency and quality thresholds
Dashboard with token-cost, p95 latency, and prompt-eval quality signals available and linked in runbook
Observed token-cost reduction >=15% for pilot traffic with p95 latency regression <=10% and eval drift <=1.5%

metrics: p95 latency regression budget: <=10% vs baseline
Eval quality drift budget: <=1.5% on tracked prompt set
Rollout success criteria: stability for 72h at target config
risks: Caching correctness edge cases causing stateful responses to diverge (mitigation: strict cache key rules and automated replay tests)
Quantization-induced quality regressions on niche prompts (mitigation: conservative quant profiles and per-prompt rollback map)
Batching increases tail latency under sudden spike patterns (mitigation: latency-aware micro-batching window and emergency fallback to unbatched path)
Customer trust erosion if Dedicated pilot impacts SLAs (mitigation: staged canary and explicit SLA guard)
decisions: Adopt conservative quantization profiles by default (int8 mixed with selective float16 for critical layers)
Implement per-route gating rather than global knobs to minimize blast radius
Use prefix/KV caching with strict immutability expectations; do not cache responses containing ephemeral tokens
post_mortem_plan: After each pilot: publish concise post-mortem summarizing cost delta, latency/quality regressions, decisions and follow-ups
Feed results into Optimize recommendation engine and update runbook with tuned presets
